summary: Assign append's result to the slice supplied as its first argument.
bad:
p.positives = append(p.negatives, x)
p.negatives = append(p.negatives, y)
good:
p.positives = append(p.positives, x)
p.negatives = append(p.negatives, y)

summary: Pass the string before the prefix in strings.HasPrefix.
Use compound assignment when updating a variable from its previous value.
Pass an argument that permits the requested operation.
Use a loop condition that agrees with its increment.
Simplify equivalent Boolean expressions.
Begin local variable and parameter identifiers with lowercase letters.
bad: func process(IN int, OUT *int) (ERR error) { return nil }
good: func process(in int, out *int) (err error) { return nil }

summary: Test specific types before interfaces that include them.
Use the standard generated-code comment format.
bad: // This file was automatically generated by foogen
good: // Code generated by foogen. DO NOT EDIT.

summary: Separate comment markers from text with a space.
Place the default switch case first or last.
bad: switch value { case 1: first(); default: other(); case 2: second() }
good: switch value { case 1: first(); case 2: second(); default: other() }

summary: Begin a deprecation notice with Deprecated:.
bad:
// deprecated, use Current instead
func Old() int { return 1 }
good:
// Deprecated: Use Current instead.
func Old() int { return 1 }

summary: Pass the intended distinct arguments to the operation.
Give different conditions the intended distinct operations.
List each switch case once.
Use the intended operands instead of repeating one expression.
Use else if instead of nesting an if directly within else.
Return from the function when deferred cleanup must run.
Register flags against variables instead of immediately copying pointer results.
good: var b bool; flag.BoolVar(&b, "b", false, "b docs")

summary: Remove unintended spaces from flag identifiers.
Use a switch for a sequence of conditional alternatives.
Remove unintended trailing spaces from map keys.
Use the zero value directly instead of dereferencing a new allocation.
Return nil explicitly after checking that an error equals nil.
Use the last valid slice index instead of the slice length.
Use regexp.MustCompile for a constant expression when discarding compilation errors.
Compare lengths against zero without a redundant negative alternative.
Return an existing interface value without asserting it to the empty interface.
bad: func convert(reader io.Reader) interface{} { return reader.(interface{}) }
good: func convert(reader io.Reader) interface{} { return reader }

summary: Omit the explicit true expression from a conditional switch.
Bind the asserted value in the type switch.
good:
switch v := v.(type) {
case int:
	return v
case point:
	return v.x + v.y
default:
	return 0
}

summary: Access struct fields and array elements without an explicit pointer dereference.
Use a function value directly when the wrapper only invokes that function.
Use an existing slice instead of slicing its complete range.
Swap values with parallel assignment.
bad:
temporary := first
first = second
second = temporary

summary: Use the operation's convenience method.
